fatal_errors: The material is incorrectly treated as a generic single-phase solid solution rather than the as-cast dual-phase FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy.
The intervention is unspecified and omits the critical intermediate-temperature aging treatments near 600°C and 750°C.
The proposed grain-refinement and nanoparticle-precipitation mechanism conflicts with the target mechanism involving L12 ordering, increased APBE, planar slip, and jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
The predicted monotonic toughness improvement misses the observed non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition and the ductility minimum after 600°C aging.
No temperature window, exposure duration, or loading conditions are defined.
No prior observations or citations support the hypothesis.
The proposed experiment is merely an untreated comparison and does not specify a result that would falsify the mechanism.
explanation: The response only broadly addresses thermal treatment of a high-entropy alloy and includes an appropriate same-alloy control in principle. It does not reconstruct the alloy state, aging-temperature window, structural mediators, or non-monotonic outcome. Its mechanism is generic and unsupported, and the experiment cannot distinguish nanoparticle strengthening from the target phase-boundary and ordering mechanism. A discriminating test would compare aging across below-550°C, approximately 600°C, 750°C, and above-750°C conditions while using TEM or TKD to determine whether dislocation pile-ups and cracks initiate at jagged FCC/B2 boundary tips, alongside measurements of L12 ordering and checks excluding impurity-segregated grain-boundary fracture.
